subject: New User for CmdStan-2.2.0: Faced problem to run an example code

messages.author: b66f7d1e154bde4b
messages.subject: New User for CmdStan-2.2.0: Faced problem to run an example code
parts:
Hi STAN users,
 
Thanks in advance. I am Deb, Statistician from Sydney, Australia.
 
I am new to CmdStan and need help to start with.
 
I am using CmdStan on Windows XP (64 Bit).
 
I have used the following steps to install and run an example code using CmdStan.
 
1. Rtools
 
I have installed Rtools for Windows from http://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools.
 
I have used the path variables:
 
C:\Rtools\bin; C:\Rtools\bin\gcc-4.6.3\bin;
 
2. CmdStan-2.2.0
 
To install CmdStan, I have used:
> tar --no-same-owner -xzf stan-2.2.0.tar.gz
 
I do not know whether I should use a path variable or not.
 
But I have used the following path variables:
 
C:\stan-2.2.0; C:\stan-2.2.0\bin;
 
3. To run an example code
 
\stan-2.2.0>make src/models/basic_estimators/bernoulli
File not found - *_inst.cpp
File not found - *_def.cpp
File not found - *.hpp
FIND: Parameter format not correct
FIND: Parameter format not correct
File not found - *.stan
File not found - *.stan
File not found - *_test.cpp
File not found - *_test.cpp
File not found - *.hpp
File not found - *.stan
g++ -I src ...... -c -O3 -o bin/stan/command/stanc.o src/stan/command/stanc.cpp
src/stan/gm/parser.hpp:169: confused by earlier errors, bailing out
cc1plus: sorry, unimplemented: 64-bit mode not compiled in
cc1plus: sorry, unimplemented: 64-bit mode not compiled in
make: *** No rule to make target 'bin/stan/command/stanc.o', needed by 'bin/stanc.exe'. Stop.
 
I have also run using the following command:
 
\stan-2.2.0>make BIT=32 src/models/basic_estimators/bernoulli
 
But I've received the same error.
 
Once again, thank you very much for the time you have given.
 
Regards,
 
Deb

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] New User for CmdStan-2.2.0: Faced problem to run an example code
parts:
Hi Deb,

Two things:
1. I think your path isn't set up correctly. Can you make sure your rtools is included before c:\Windows\system32? It looks like the build process is using Windows' find.exe instead of the one packaged by rtools.
2. Add .exe to the end of your make target. It should look like:
>make src/models/basic_estimators/bernoulli.exe
(if you have a newer machine, you might want to add " -j2" or however many cores you have, if you have a lot of ram)

Can you let us know if that works?

Daniel
